mainTopic: How far דיו limits a קל וחומר: the proof from the semen of a זב, the ברייתא about a mat made impure by a מת, the גזירה שוה of 'garment and leather', and why שן ורגל is exempt in רשות הרבים
overview: This amud opens in the middle of a quoted משנה, which lists the fluids of a זב that make things טמא by touching and by carrying. The גמרא uses that list to show that the שכבת זרע of a זב is learned from רוק by a קל וחומר, with no limit from דיו. It defends this proof from the order of the list. רב אחא מדפתי then challenges רבינא with a ברייתא. In that ברייתא, a קל וחומר seems to make a mat (מפץ) טמא from a מת for seven days, even though דיו could have limited it to impurity until evening. אביי answers that the קל וחומר only teaches about a שרץ, and that the mat's impurity from a מת comes from a גזירה שוה on the words 'garment and leather'. The גמרא shows that these words are extra on both sides, and רבא uses a פסוק to show that anything made impure by a מת stays impure for seven days. Finally, the גמרא returns to damages. It rejects a קל וחומר that would make שן ורגל liable in רשות הרבים, because the פסוק says 'in the field of another'.

steps.title: The list of fluids that make things impure by touching and carrying
steps.stepSummary: The quoted משנה lists זובו, רוקו, שכבת זרעו and מי רגליו of a זב, together with דם הנדה. All of these are מטמא both במגע and במשא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The זוב of a זב, his spit, his semen, his urine, and the blood of a נדה all make things impure both by touching and by carrying.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its quote of a משנה. It brings the משנה to show that the שכבת זרע of a זב makes things impure even by carrying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The important detail is that שכבת זרע appears in this severe list, which includes being מטמא במשא. Normally semen only makes things impure by touching. So the משנה seems to give it the stricter rule of רוק, without any limit from דיו.

keyTerms.meaning: A man with an impure bodily discharge, who is a source of טומאה
The discharge of a זב itself
Touching; becoming impure by contact
Carrying; becoming impure by lifting or moving, even without touching
Menstrual blood

phrases.english: The discharge of a zav, and his spittle,
and his semen, and his urine,
and the blood of a menstruating woman –
impart impurity both by touching and by carrying.

steps.triggerLanguage: זוֹבוֹ שֶׁל זָב, וְרוּקּוֹ, וְשִׁכְבַת זַרְעוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a משנה quoted just before this section, as a source about the שכבת זרע of a זב.
steps.raayaObject: That שכבת זרע of a זב is מטמא במשא, as a full result of the קל וחומר from רוק.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה listing the fluids of a זב that are מטמא במגע ובמשא.

steps.title: Maybe it is only because of hidden drops of discharge
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that semen of a זב may be in the list only because it always comes out with tiny drops of זיבה, not because of its own status.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe here too the reason is that it is impossible for it to come out without tiny drops of זיבה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. It says the משנה might have a different reason for being strict.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the semen is impure במשא only because it is mixed with tiny drops of זוב, then the strictness comes from the זוב itself. In that case nothing is learned from רוק, so the משנה proves nothing about a קל וחומר or about דיו.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps; maybe (opens another way to read the source)
Tiny drops of זוב discharge
It is impossible

phrases.english: But perhaps here too –
phrases.notes: 'Here too' means using the same kind of explanation the גמרא offered just before.

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר בְּלֹא צִחְצוּחֵי זִיבָה!
phrases.english: it is because it is impossible without small drops of ziva!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from the משנה in step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof drawn from the משנה, not the rule in the משנה itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The strictness could come from drops of זוב mixed in, not from a קל וחומר from רוק.

steps.title: The order of the list shows it is learned from spittle
steps.stepSummary: If the reason were drops of זוב, the משנה would have placed semen next to זובו. Since it places it next to רוקו, the rule must come from רוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let the משנה list it next to his זוב. Why is it listed next to his spit? It must be because its rule comes from his spit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the original proof by looking at where semen appears in the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The place of an item in the משנה's list tells us its source. Semen is placed right after רוקו, so its strictness is learned from רוק. That means the semen itself is מטמא במשא, even without drops of זוב, and the proof stands.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (opens a reply that shows a suggestion does not fit)
What is different? Why this way and not another?
Because it is derived from his spittle

steps.whatToRemember: The proof holds: semen of a זב is מטמא במשא because it is learned from רוק by a קל וחומר, and here דיו did not limit it.

phrases.english: If so, let him teach it next to his discharge;

phrases.aramaic: מַאי שְׁנָא דְּקָתָנֵי לַהּ גַּבֵּי רוּקּוֹ?
phrases.english: what is different that he teaches it next to his spittle?
Rather, it is because it comes from his spittle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the rejection in step 2 and brings back the proof of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proof from the order of items in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Semen is strict only because of the drops of זוב mixed into it.
steps.terutzMaskana: Semen is listed next to רוקו because its strictness is learned from רוק.

steps.title: רב אחא: here is a תנא who ignores the limit even when it is harmless
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא מדפתי challenges רבינא. There is a תנא who does not apply דיו at all, even when applying it would not cancel the קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא מדפתי said to רבינא: But this תנא does not use דיו, even though using it would not destroy the קל וחומר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the main question about דיו. רב אחא מדפתי announces a challenge, and he will prove it in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier idea was that a תנא who rejects דיו does so only where it would cancel the קל וחומר. Where it would not cancel it, the תנא would still use it. רב אחא claims there is a תנא who drops דיו even where it would cause no harm.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is enough': what is learned from a קל וחומר cannot be stricter than its source
An argument from a lighter case to a stricter case
Is refuted or cancelled
A sage of the משנה period

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases. When דיו would 'destroy' a קל וחומר, the argument would teach nothing at all. Here, applying דיו would still leave the argument teaching something, which is why rejecting it is surprising.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא מִדִּפְתִּי לְרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: Rav Aḥa of Difti said to Ravina:

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא הַאי תַּנָּא לָא דָּרֵישׁ דַּיּוֹ,
phrases.english: But this tanna does not apply 'it is sufficient',

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא מִפְּרִיךְ קַל וָחוֹמֶר!
phrases.english: even though it would not refute the a fortiori inference!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא מִדִּפְתִּי לְרָבִינָא: וְהָא הַאי תַּנָּא לָא דָּרֵישׁ דַּיּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion about semen and returns to the main discussion of דיו.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that a tanna who rejects דיו still uses it wherever it would not cancel the קל וחומר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא shows a תנא taking a קל וחומר to its full extent, even though limiting it would still leave a useful result.

steps.title: The ברייתא: a mat becomes impure from a corpse
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא derives with a קל וחומר that a מפץ becomes טמא from a מת. Small clay jugs are not made טמא by a זב, yet they become טמא from a מת. A mat, which is made טמא by a זב, should surely become טמא from a מת.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: How do we know that a mat becomes impure from a מת? It is logical: small jugs, which stay pure from a זב, become impure from a מת. A mat, which does become impure from a זב, should surely become impure from a מת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא that is the basis of רב אחא's challenge. It sets up the קל וחומר that he will examine in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument compares two kinds of טומאה. Small jugs are 'stronger' against a זב, since they stay pure, but they still become impure from a מת. So the mat, which is 'weaker' against a זב, must become impure from a מת as well.

keyTerms.meaning: A mat, which a זב can make impure by lying or sitting on it
Small clay jugs
It is logical (opens a קל וחומר)
A dead body, the most severe source of טומאה

phrases.english: As it is taught: From where do we know that a mat becomes impure with a corpse?
And it is a logical derivation:
Just as small jugs – which are pure with a zav,
phrases.notes: Clay pots become impure only from the inside, and these openings are too narrow for a זב to reach in.

phrases.english: become impure with a corpse;
phrases.notes: Meaning when they are under the same roof as the body.

phrases.english: a mat – which becomes impure with a zav,
is it not logical that it should become impure with a corpse?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source for רב אחא's claim in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: That there is a תנא who does not apply דיו even when it would not cancel the קל וחומר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא deriving that a מפץ becomes טמא from a מת by a קל וחומר from פכין קטנים.

steps.title: Why seven days? The limit should have allowed only one day
steps.stepSummary: The תנא uses the קל וחומר to make the mat impure for seven days. But he could have let the קל וחומר give only impurity until evening, as with a זב, and used דיו to rule out seven days.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he uses it both for impurity until evening and for seven-day impurity. Why? Say that the קל וחומר works for impurity until evening, and דיו works to rule out seven-day impurity!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא finishes his challenge. He shows that the ברייתא drew a full seven-day impurity from the קל וחומר, when דיו could have limited it without cancelling the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source of the argument is the mat's impurity from a זב, which lasts only until evening. Applying דיו would still leave the קל וחומר teaching something: that the mat becomes impure from a מת at all, until evening. Since the תנא still gives seven days, he does not apply דיו even where it causes no harm.

keyTerms.meaning: Impurity that lasts until nightfall
Seven-day impurity, the kind caused by a מת
Let it be effective; let it accomplish
To exclude

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a case where דיו is not applied even though it would not empty out the קל וחומר. That breaks the clean rule set up earlier, and the גמרא will need to answer it.

phrases.english: And he cites it both for impurity until nightfall,
and for impurity of seven days.
And why?

phrases.aramaic: אֵימָא: אַהֲנִי קַל וָחוֹמֶר לְטוּמְאַת עֶרֶב,
phrases.english: Say: let the a fortiori inference be effective for impurity until nightfall,
and let 'it is sufficient' be effective to exclude seven-day impurity!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקָמַיְיתֵי לַהּ בֵּין לְטוּמְאַת עֶרֶב, בֵּין לְטוּמְאַת שִׁבְעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the ברייתא of step 5 supports the challenge of step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that דיו is always applied where it would not cancel the קל וחומר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Limiting the result to impurity until evening would keep the קל וחומר useful, yet the תנא gives seven days, so he does not apply דיו here.

steps.title: אביי's answer: the קל וחומר is really about a שרץ
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that אביי already dealt with this question. The קל וחומר in the ברייתא teaches that a mat becomes טמא from a שרץ, not from a מת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to him: רב נחמן בר זכריה already asked this to אביי, and אביי answered: the תנא learns it from a mat with a שרץ. This is what he means: From where do we know that a mat becomes impure from a שרץ? It is logical. Small clay jugs stay pure from a זב, yet become impure from a שרץ. A mat becomes impure from a זב, so surely it becomes impure from a שרץ!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא defends himself by quoting אביי. The ברייתא's קל וחומר is about a שרץ, not about a מת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Impurity from a שרץ only lasts until evening, just like impurity from a זב. So applying דיו here changes nothing, and the question from step 6 ('why did he not use דיו to limit it?') disappears. The seven-day impurity from a מת must come from somewhere else, and the next step shows where.

keyTerms.meaning: The dead body of a creeping animal, which makes things טמא until evening
Small clay jugs
'And it is logical', the opening words of a קל וחומר
He raised this question (or contradiction) to him

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא in step 5 seemed to be teaching about a מת. אביי is saying that the קל וחומר part is really about a שרץ, and the מת part is learned separately.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: רבינא is answering רב אחא מדפתי.

phrases.english: This question was already raised
by Rav Nachman bar Zecharya to Abaye,
and Abaye said to him:
The tanna derives it from a mat with a creeping animal,
and this is what he is saying:
From where do we know that a mat becomes impure from a creeping animal?
And it is a logical inference:
Just as small jugs,
which stay pure from a zav, become impure from a creeping animal;
a mat, which becomes impure from a zav,
is it not logical that it should become impure from a creeping animal?

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר ליה כבר רמא ניהליה רב נחמן בר זכריה לאביי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of steps 4–6 by reading the ברייתא's קל וחומר as teaching about a שרץ, not a מת.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the source: the קל וחומר is about a different subject, where דיו makes no difference
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא used a קל וחומר from זב to give a mat the full seven-day impurity of a מת, and ignored דיו.
steps.terutzMaskana: The קל וחומר only teaches impurity from a שרץ, which lasts until evening anyway, so there is no proof against דיו.

steps.title: A mat becomes impure from a מת through a גזירה שוה
steps.stepSummary: The second part of the ברייתא learns the impurity of a mat from a מת through a גזירה שוה. The same words, 'garment and leather', appear in the פסוקים about שרץ and about מת.
steps.simpleTranslation: But from where do we know that a mat becomes impure from a מת? 'Garment and leather' is said about שרץ, and 'garment and leather' is said about מת. Just as a mat becomes impure under 'garment and leather' in the case of שרץ, so too a mat becomes impure under 'garment and leather' in the case of מת.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי continues his reading of the ברייתא. The seven-day impurity of a mat from a מת comes from a word-link between פסוקים, not from the קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First the קל וחומר established that a mat counts as 'garment and leather' for שרץ. Now the גזירה שוה carries that over to מת. A גזירה שוה is not a קל וחומר, so דיו does not apply, and the mat gets the full impurity of a מת.

keyTerms.meaning: Learning one law from another because the same word appears in both
'Garment and leather', the shared words that make the link
A human corpse, which makes things טמא for seven days

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the ברייתא gives the mat seven days of impurity without breaking the rule of דיו.

phrases.english: But from where do we know that a mat becomes impure from a corpse?
"Garment and leather" is stated regarding a creeping animal,
and "garment and leather" is stated regarding a corpse;
just as with "garment and leather" stated regarding a creeping animal,
a mat becomes impure from it,
so too with "garment and leather" stated regarding a corpse,
a mat becomes impure from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's two-part reading. After the קל וחומר for שרץ, the גזירה שוה carries the rule over to מת.
steps.raayaObject: That a mat becomes impure from a מת
steps.raayaSupportSource: A גזירה שוה from the words בגד ועור in the פסוקים of שרץ and מת

steps.title: The גזירה שוה only works if the words are extra
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the גזירה שוה must use extra words (מופנה). Otherwise someone could argue that שרץ is stricter than מת, since a שרץ makes things impure with only a lentil-sized piece.
steps.simpleTranslation: The words must be free. Because if they are not free, the link can be refuted: What about שרץ? It makes things impure with a lentil-sized piece. Can you say the same about a מת, which does not make things impure with a lentil-sized piece, only with an olive-sized piece?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a weakness in the גזירה שוה from step 8. It holds up only if the words 'garment and leather' are extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A normal גזירה שוה can be broken if one side has a special strictness. A שרץ is stricter than a מת, because a tiny lentil-sized piece already makes things טמא. So maybe a mat becomes impure only from the stricter שרץ. If the words are extra (מופנה), this kind of attack does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Free', meaning the words are extra and were put there for the גזירה שוה
To refute, to knock down a comparison
The size of a lentil, the amount of a שרץ that makes things impure
The size of an olive, the amount of a מת that makes things impure

phrases.english: It must be free;
phrases.notes: 'Free' means the words are extra in their own פסוק, so they are there to teach the גזירה שוה.

phrases.english: for if it is not free,
one could refute it:
What about a creeping animal? It is special because it makes impure with a lentil-bulk;
will you say the same about a corpse,
which does not make impure with a lentil-bulk, but only with an olive-bulk?

steps.triggerLanguage: מופנה דאי לא מופנה איכא למפרך
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the גזירה שוה from step 8 and shows it needs extra words to stand.
steps.kashyaTarget: The גזירה שוה of בגד ועור between שרץ and מת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A שרץ has a strictness that a מת lacks (lentil-size versus olive-size), so the comparison could be broken unless the words are extra.

steps.title: Proof that the words are extra
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא confirms that the words are extra. The Torah links שרץ to שכבת זרע by placing them side by side, and the פסוק about שכבת זרע already says 'every garment and all leather'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, they are certainly free. Since שרץ is compared to שכבת זרע, as it is written, 'or a man from whom [semen] goes out', and next to it, 'or a man who touches any שרץ'; and it is written about שכבת זרע, 'and every garment and all leather on which there is semen'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins proving that 'garment and leather' are extra. It shows that שרץ and שכבת זרע are placed side by side in the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the two are placed next to each other (a היקש), what is said about one applies to the other. The פסוק about שכבת זרע already mentions 'garment and leather'. So the גמרא is building toward showing that these words are not needed in their own place for שרץ, which would make them free for the גזירה שוה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Indeed', a word confirming the point
Was compared (by היקש, placing two laws side by side)
Semen, which makes things impure until evening
And placed right next to it

phrases.english: Indeed, it is certainly free:
Now, since a creeping animal is compared to semen,
as it is written: "Or a man from whom [semen] goes out, etc."
and right next to it:
"Or a man who touches any creeping animal";
and it is written about semen:
"And every garment and all leather
on which there is semen."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the concern of step 9 by beginning to show that 'garment and leather' are extra words.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the words are extra because of a היקש between שרץ and שכבת זרע
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The words בגד ועור by שרץ might be needed for their own law, which would leave the גזירה שוה open to refutation.
steps.terutzMaskana: שרץ is linked to שכבת זרע, whose פסוק already says 'garment and leather', so the words by שרץ are free for the גזירה שוה.

steps.title: The words in the שרץ section are extra
steps.stepSummary: Since שרץ is already linked to שכבת זרע, which mentions garment and leather, the words 'garment and leather' written about שרץ must be extra. They are there to be used for the גזירה שוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does the Torah need to write 'garment and leather' about a שרץ? Learn from this that the words are there to be 'free' (extra) for the גזירה שוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer from the last step. It says the words 'garment and leather' in the שרץ section are not needed for their own law, so they are free to be used for the גזירה שוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know from שכבת זרע that garments and leather become impure, and שרץ is placed right next to it. So writing those words again about שרץ adds nothing new, which means they must be there to teach the גזירה שוה. This solves the worry from step 9 that someone could argue שרץ is stricter than מת.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? (this suggests the words are extra)
Learn from it
To make it 'free,' meaning left open for a גזירה שוה
Free or extra; words not needed for anything else

phrases.english: 'Garment and leather' that the Merciful One wrote about a creeping animal –
why do I need it?
phrases.notes: We already know it from שכבת זרע, which sits right next to שרץ in the Torah.

phrases.english: Learn from it: it is there to be free (extra).

steps.triggerLanguage: ״בֶּגֶד וָעוֹר״ דִּכְתַב רַחֲמָנָא בְּשֶׁרֶץ – לְמָה לִי? שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ לְאַפְנוֹיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer of step 10 by drawing its conclusion.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The words 'garment and leather' in the שרץ section are extra, so they can be used for the גזירה שוה.

steps.title: Extra on only one side is not enough for everyone
steps.stepSummary: The words are extra only in the שרץ section, not in the מת section. That is fine for the view that such a גזירה שוה cannot be argued against, but not for the view that it can.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the words are still extra on only one side! That works for the one who says a גזירה שוה that is extra on one side is learned and cannot be argued against. But for the one who says we learn from it and can still argue against it, what can we say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back. It says the words are extra on only one side of the גזירה שוה, and some opinions say that is not strong enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזירה שוה has two sides, here שרץ and מת. So far only the שרץ side is shown to be extra. One opinion says one extra side is enough to block any logical argument, but another opinion says we can still argue against it, and then the argument from step 9 that שרץ is stricter comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: From one side (only one of the two פסוקים has extra words)
We learn from it and cannot argue against it
We learn from it, but a logical argument can still knock it down
This works well (setting up a 'but what about...')

steps.confusionAlert: Both opinions agree you can learn from a one-sided extra גזירה שוה. They argue only about whether a logical argument can still knock it down.

phrases.english: But still, it is free from only one side!
phrases.notes: The words are extra in the שרץ section, but nothing has been said yet about the מת section.

phrases.english: This works well according to the one who says
that a גזירה שוה free from one side –
we learn from it and cannot argue against it – fine;
but according to the one who says
we learn from it and can argue against it,
what is there to say?
phrases.notes: We could again argue that שרץ is stricter, since a lentil-sized piece makes things impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of step 11 as not being strong enough.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the גזירה שוה is safe because the שרץ words are extra
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only one side is extra. According to the view of לְמֵידִין וּמְשִׁיבִין, the argument that שרץ is stricter could still break the גזירה שוה.

steps.title: The words in the מת section are extra too
steps.stepSummary: מת is linked by the Torah to שכבת זרע, which already mentions garment and leather. So the words in the מת section are extra as well, and the גזירה שוה is extra on both sides.
steps.simpleTranslation: The words about מת are also extra. After all, מת is compared to שכבת זרע, as it says 'one who touches anything impure from a dead person, or a man from whom semen goes out.' And about שכבת זרע it says 'every garment and all leather that has semen on it.' So why does the Torah need 'garment and leather' about מת? Learn that they are extra, and the גזירה שוה is extra on both sides.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the מת side is extra too. It uses the same method it used for שרץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One פסוק puts מת and שכבת זרע side by side, so whatever is said about שכבת זרע applies to מת. Since שכבת זרע already mentions garment and leather, writing them again for מת is extra. Now both sides are extra, so no logical argument can knock down the גזירה שוה according to any opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: After all; since
Is compared (by being placed together in a פסוק)
Impure from a dead body
Extra on both sides, the strongest kind of גזירה שוה

steps.whatToRemember: Both the שרץ words and the מת words are extra, because each is linked to שכבת זרע. So the גזירה שוה is extra on both sides and cannot be argued against.

phrases.english: The words about a dead body are also free –
since a dead body is compared to semen,
as it is written:
'And one who touches anything impure from a dead person,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אִישׁ אֲשֶׁר תֵּצֵא מִמֶּנּוּ וְגוֹ׳״;
phrases.english: or a man from whom [semen] goes out, etc.';
and it is written about semen:
'And every garment and all leather
that has semen on it';
'Garment and leather' that the Merciful One wrote about a dead body –
why do I need it?
Learn from it: it is there to be free,
and so it is free from both sides.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the other side of the גזירה שוה is also extra
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought only the שרץ words were extra, so the גזירה שוה could be argued against.
steps.terutzMaskana: The מת words are also extra through its link to שכבת זרע, so the גזירה שוה is extra on both sides.

steps.title: Do the details come along with the גזירה שוה?
steps.stepSummary: If we learn only the basic law and keep the details of מת, the mat is impure for seven days. But if we also learn the details from the source, the mat should be impure only until evening, like with a שרץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: That works for the one who says: learn from it, and then set it in its own place. But for the one who says: learn from it, and learn the details from it too, what can we say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new problem. It asks how long the mat stays impure from a מת, based on a debate about how a גזירה שוה works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One view says a גזירה שוה only moves the basic law, and the details follow the new place. So a mat touched by a מת is impure for seven days, like other things impure from a מת. The other view says the details move too, so the mat would be impure only until evening, like with a שרץ, and that goes against the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn the law from it, but set its details in their own place
Learn the law from it, and the details from it too
What is there to say? (a challenge that needs an answer; רבא answers it in the next step)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not asking whether the mat becomes impure from a מת. That is settled. The question is only how long it stays impure.

phrases.english: This works well according to the one who says:
learn from it – and set it in its own place;
phrases.notes: Learn only that the mat becomes impure; how long it lasts follows the rules of מת, which is seven days.

phrases.english: but according to the one who says:
learn from it, and from it too,
phrases.notes: Take the details from the source too, so the impurity would last only until evening, like a שרץ.

phrases.english: what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר: דּוּן מִינַּהּ – וְאוֹקֵי בְּאַתְרַאּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the גזירה שוה stands, asks a new question about how long the impurity lasts.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that a mat touched by a מת is impure for seven days
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to דּוּן מִינַּהּ וּמִינַּהּ, the details come from שרץ, so the mat should be impure only until evening, not seven days.

steps.title: רבא: Anything made impure by a corpse stays impure at least seven days
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers the challenge from Step 14. Once the mat can become impure through a מת, a פסוק teaches that every impurity from a מת lasts at least seven days, so the mat is impure for seven days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The verse says, 'And you shall wash your garments on the seventh day.' This teaches that every impurity you get from a dead body must last no less than seven days.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge: even if the mat takes its details from שרץ, it still stays impure for seven days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge said that if the mat gets its details from שרץ, its impurity should end in the evening. רבא says the length of impurity is not a detail learned from the source. It is a fixed rule of טומאת מת: anything a מת makes impure stays impure for at least seven days.

keyTerms.meaning: Impurity that comes from a dead body
Less than seven (days)

steps.whatToRemember: The mat becomes impure through a מת, and every impurity from a מת lasts at least seven days. So the mat is impure for seven days, whatever details it learns from שרץ.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that even under the view דּוּן מִינַּהּ וּמִינַּהּ, where details come along with a גזירה שוה, the Torah's fixed seven-day rule for anything made impure by a מת still applies. That is how the ברייתא can give the mat seven days.

phrases.english: Rava said: The verse says:
"And you shall wash your garments on the seventh day"
all impurities that you become impure with through a corpse
shall not be less than seven (days).

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבא, אמר קרא: וכבסתם בגדיכם ביום השביעי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 14 about the mat being impure only until evening.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A פסוק sets a fixed minimum length for all טומאת מת, so the source cannot shorten it.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the mat learns its details from שרץ, its impurity should end in the evening.
steps.terutzMaskana: Any impurity that comes from a מת lasts at least seven days, so the mat is impure for seven days.

steps.title: Should שן ורגל be liable in רשות הרבים, learned from קרן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to damages. It suggests a קל וחומר: קרן pays only half in the victim's property yet is liable in רשות הרבים, so שן ורגל, which pays in full in the victim's property, should surely be liable in רשות הרבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let שן ורגל be liable in the public domain through a קל וחומר. קרן pays only half damage in the injured person's property, and still it is liable in the public domain. שן ורגל pay full damage in the injured person's property, so isn't it logical that they are liable in the public domain?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the mat discussion and returns to damages. It builds a קל וחומר to make שן ורגל liable in רשות הרבים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קרן seems weaker, since it pays only half damage in רשות הניזק, yet it is liable in רשות הרבים. שן ורגל seems stronger, since it pays full damage in רשות הניזק. So logic says the stronger case should be liable wherever the weaker one is.

keyTerms.meaning: Damage by an animal eating (tooth) or trampling (foot)
Damage by goring (horn)
The public domain
The property of the injured party
Half the cost of the damage
Logical argument: if the weaker case has a rule, the stronger case surely does too

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'pays full damage' with 'liable everywhere'. The question here is about WHERE the owner is liable, not HOW MUCH he pays.

phrases.english: And let Eating and Trampling be liable
in the public domain, through a קל וחומר
And if Goring, which on the property of the injured party
pays only half damage
is liable in the public domain;
Eating and Trampling, which on the property of the injured party
pays full damage
is it not logical that it is liable in the public domain?

steps.triggerLanguage: ותהא שן ורגל חייב ברשות הרבים מקל וחומר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the דיו and mat discussion and returns to the damages topic of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that שן ורגל is exempt in רשות הרבים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קרן is weaker in רשות הניזק (half damage) but still liable in רשות הרבים, so שן ורגל, which is stronger there (full damage), should also be liable in רשות הרבים.

steps.title: The פסוק limits שן ורגל to another's field
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the קל וחומר. The פסוק says 'and it consumed in another's field', which teaches that שן ורגל is liable only there and not in רשות הרבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And it consumed in the field of another', and not in the public domain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the קל וחומר with a פסוק that limits שן ורגל to someone else's field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר cannot override what the Torah says outright. The words 'in the field of another' limit liability for שן ורגל to the victim's property, so there is no liability in רשות הרבים.

keyTerms.meaning: And it consumed; the Torah's word for damage by שן ורגל
Another person's field

steps.whatToRemember: שן ורגל is exempt in רשות הרבים because the Torah says 'in the field of another', even though a קל וחומר from קרן might suggest otherwise.

phrases.english: The verse says: "And it consumed in the field of another"
and not in the public domain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the קל וחומר of Step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A פסוק rules out what the קל וחומר would have taught.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שן ורגל should be liable in רשות הרבים because of the קל וחומר from קרן.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Torah limits שן ורגל to 'another's field', so there is no liability in רשות הרבים.
